intro: The Rams will play without Puka Nacua for months, the Lions go on without Aidan Hutchinson, and Jonah Coleman and Jaxon Smith-Njigba both put up huge lines in Week 11. Thanksgiving week opens with Kansas City at Buffalo on Thursday night. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Puka Nacua out two months after MCL surgery, plus a three-game suspension
top.dek: Nacua had surgery on an MCL injury last week, and Sean McVay says he will miss a couple of months. The NFL also suspended him three games for a personal conduct violation, and he can return Dec. 14. The Rams are 6-4 and have won four straight.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lions lose Aidan Hutchinson for the season and Jack Campbell indefinitely
top.dek: Hutchinson hurt his right knee celebrating a sack against New England, and an AP source says the injury ends his year. Rookie Derrick Moore is the first option to replace him. Linebacker Jack Campbell has a severe neck injury with no return date.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Rookie Jonah Coleman runs for 111 yards and three touchdowns in Denver
top.dek: Coleman carried 24 times and added four catches for 18 yards in the 38-24 win over the Raiders. It was his first 100-yard game. He is the first Broncos rookie with that rushing line since Clinton Portis in 2002.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 144: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's receiving yards in one quarter, a Seahawks record
top.dek: Smith-Njigba piled up 144 yards in the third quarter against the Raiders and finished with 171. Seattle won 21-13. The Seahawks are 4-0 in games Drew Lock has played this season.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Chiefs visit Bills in Buffalo's first home Thanksgiving game
top.dek: Kansas City plays at 9-1 Buffalo on Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch whether Josh Allen runs: he had no carries against Miami, and the Chiefs say they are preparing for him to scramble.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills defense keeps opponents out of the end zone

stories.text: Bills defense shuts out the touchdown column again
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Miami 26-9 on Sunday and gave up only three field goals. No opponent has reached the end zone against the Bills in 15 straight quarters. The team has not allowed a touchdown in 43 consecutive drives, the longest single-season streak in the NFL since the 2019 Patriots.

stories.text: Benford, Kincaid and Williams still unsettled before Chiefs
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore hyperextended his left knee late in the first half Sunday but returned and finished with 8 catches for 91 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback Christian Benford (groin), tight end Dalton Kincaid (hand) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) all missed the Miami game, and a Benford return Thursday looks like a long shot.

stories.text: Greg Rousseau hits double digits in sacks
stories.summary: Rousseau sacked Miami twice and now has 10 sacks through 10 games, a career high. He has four multi-sack games, more than any other player in the league this season. No Bill had that many sacks through the first 10 games of a season since Lorenzo Alexander in 2016.

stories.text: 9.3: points per game the Bills defense has allowed since Week 8
stories.summary: That mark leads the NFL over the stretch. Buffalo also leads in yards allowed per game (220.8) and third-down rate allowed (16.7%) in that span. Through the first seven weeks, the same unit gave up 28.5 points per game.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Highmark on Thanksgiving night
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Kansas City on Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, the first home Thanksgiving game in team history. The Bills are 9-1 and have won six straight. Watch whether Josh Allen runs: he had no carries against Miami, and the Chiefs say they are preparing for him to scramble.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins lose a fourth straight and three linemen

stories.text: Dolphins fall to 1-9 with a 26-9 loss in Buffalo
stories.summary: Miami lost its fourth straight game and scored only on three field goals from kicker Daniel Carlson. The Dolphins finished with 185 total yards, their lowest of the season. Coach Jeff Hafley pointed to the third-down failures after the game.

stories.text: Three defensive linemen done for the year
stories.summary: Miami lost Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers to season-ending injuries. Starting quarterback Malik Willis is on injured reserve, which put Kyle McCord back under center. The Dolphins also played Sunday without their top three defensive tackles and their starting safety, per local reports.

stories.text: Kyle McCord struggles in his second NFL start
stories.summary: McCord completed 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards with one interception and took two sacks. He called it his worst day as a pro and said he could have been a lot better. Malik Washington led Miami with three catches for 30 yards.

stories.text: 2 for 14: Miami's third-down day in Buffalo
stories.summary: The Dolphins converted 14 percent of their third downs against the Bills. Entering the game, Miami ranked 12th in the league at 40.2 percent. Hafley said that kind of day will not get it done.

stories.text: Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium for a bottom-feeder duel
stories.summary: Miami hosts the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Miami is 1-9 and the Jets are 3-8. Watch whether the Dolphins can protect McCord and move the chains on third down.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Tommy DeVito will start with Maye out

stories.text: DeVito to start for Patriots after Maye's injury
stories.summary: Coach Mike Vrabel confirmed Monday that Tommy DeVito will start at the Chargers on Nov. 29. Drake Maye is expected to miss the rest of the season, and Behren Morton is the only other quarterback on the roster. New England sits at 5-5 coming off its bye.

stories.text: Maye's leg injury leaves a long list on IR
stories.summary: Maye was hurt on a sack by Aidan Hutchinson in Munich, and early reports of an ankle injury later pointed to a fractured fibula. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) may return to practice, and receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) becomes eligible to return after the bye. Running back TreVeyon Henderson and tackle Mike Onwenu are also on injured reserve.

stories.text: Elijah Ponder leads the pass rush
stories.summary: Ponder has a team-high 7.5 sacks and 32 pressures through ten games. Rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas has 28 pressures and 14 run stuffs. The Patriots rank sixth in the league in pressure rate at 38.8 percent.

stories.text: 151: total yards New England managed against Detroit
stories.summary: DeVito finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception after Maye left the 35-10 loss. Before the injury, Maye had 2,330 passing yards and 18 touchdowns. That output now leaves the offense with a large gap to fill.

stories.text: Patriots head west to face the Chargers
stories.summary: New England plays at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chargers are 1-9. Watch DeVito's first start of the year and how the line holds up with Vera-Tucker and Onwenu still in question.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets edge Chargers to snap a losing streak

stories.text: Jets beat the Chargers 27-24 on the road
stories.summary: New York never trailed in Los Angeles and moved to 3-8. The Jets gained 341 yards without punting. Breece Hall's touchdown ended a nine-quarter scoring drought, and the team scored its first touchdown since Week 8.

stories.text: Geno Smith's ankle holds up after scare against Buffalo
stories.summary: Smith hurt his left ankle in the Nov. 15 loss to Buffalo, and imaging showed no major injury. He started against the Chargers and played well in the first half. The Jets did not report new injuries from Sunday's game.

stories.text: Geno Smith throws three touchdowns on 21 attempts
stories.summary: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three scores. Veteran Sterling Shepard caught two touchdowns on two receptions for 26 yards. Hall added 86 rushing yards on 20 carries and Braelon Allen ran for 75.

stories.text: 6: sacks the Jets defense recorded on Justin Herbert
stories.summary: Rookie David Bailey had two of them. Herbert still went 15 of 21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. The Jets held on after the Chargers cut the margin to three points with about two minutes left.

stories.text: Jets visit Miami, then get a bye
stories.summary: New York plays at the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Miami is 1-9 and has lost four straight. The Jets then have their bye in Week 13.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens lose a sixth straight, 35-33

stories.text: Ravens lose a sixth straight after late collapse in Carolina
stories.summary: Baltimore took a 33-32 lead on Derrick Henry's 15-yard touchdown run with 6:12 left, then watched Carolina march 55 yards in 12 plays for the go-ahead field goal. Jacoby Brissett threw an interception with 36 seconds left to seal the 35-33 loss and drop the Ravens to 4-7. Coach Jesse Minter blamed himself for not holding the lead, while Kyle Hamilton said the players have to execute.

stories.text: Madubuike and Hawkins sat out, Humphrey deactivated
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) were ruled out against Carolina, and cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated with no injury listed. The Ravens missed Madubuike against the run as Chuba Hubbard piled up 120 yards. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane (shoulder) was cleared to play.

stories.text: Mike Green piles up sacks again in a losing effort
stories.summary: Edge rusher Mike Green recorded two sacks for the second straight game against Carolina. Cornerback T.J. Tampa also stepped in for Humphrey and picked off Bryce Young in the end zone. Neither play was enough to stop the sixth straight defeat.

stories.text: 338-183: Ravens outgained Carolina in the first half and still lost
stories.summary: Baltimore held a 338 to 183 yardage edge at halftime and led 26-22. Turnovers and special teams errors erased it. Justice Hill fumbled out of the end zone for a touchback, Henry lost a fumble, and LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts. The Ravens have also allowed at least 33 points in four of their last five games.

stories.text: Ravens visit Houston, then get a bye
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at the 4-6 Houston Texans on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at NRG Stadium, then has its Week 13 bye. Watch the run defense and whether Madubuike returns, since Carolina ran for 147 yards.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals lose 22-20 on last-second kick

stories.text: Commanders beat Bengals 22-20 on a walk-off field goal
stories.summary: Evan McPherson's 56-yard field goal put Cincinnati up 20-19 with 46 seconds left. Washington then covered 64 yards in three plays, and Drew Stevens kicked a 26-yard winner as time expired. The loss ended the Bengals' five-game winning streak and dropped them to 7-3. A clock operator error left two seconds on the board that never ran, though it likely did not change the result.

stories.text: Risner out with knee injury, Cook shakes off ankle scare
stories.summary: Right guard Dalton Risner missed the game with a knee injury, and Jalen Rivers started in his place. Safety Bryan Cook had an ankle scare but returned. Safety Dax Hill, who battled illness during the week, spent the final two drives on the sideline.

stories.text: Burrow throws for 300 yards and no turnovers in the loss
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 28 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. Tee Higgins caught two passes for 43 yards and a score, but Ja'Marr Chase managed five catches for 31 yards on nine targets. Burrow also missed Chase deep in the third quarter.

stories.text: 31: Rushing yards for the Bengals against Washington
stories.summary: Cincinnati's run game produced just 31 yards, and a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak near midfield early in the game got stuffed. The offense still put up 300 passing yards but could not control the clock late. Boye Mafe had three first-half sacks and now has 9.5 on the season.

stories.text: Bengals host New Orleans on Sunday
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Paycor Stadium. Watch the right guard spot with Risner's knee in question and whether the defense tightens up in the closing minutes after Monday's collapse.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns hit the bye at 6-4 on tight wins

stories.text: Browns reach the bye at 6-4 with every win by four or fewer
stories.summary: Cleveland beat Houston 27-24 on Nov. 15 after trailing 17-0, and all six of its wins have come by four points or fewer. NFL research says no team has ever opened a season that way. The Browns hold the last AFC wild-card spot, and Todd Monken says he is taking it day by day.

stories.text: No official report on the bye, but a few names to watch
stories.summary: The Browns did not release an injury report this week. Defensive end Derek Barnett left the Houston game with a hamstring injury, and receiver Denzel Boston is dealing with a toe issue. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger has played through an ankle injury since Oct. 11, and Ronnie Hickman (concussion) returned to practice.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson strings together a third straight 300-yard game
stories.summary: Watson threw for 312 yards on 25 of 40 passing against Houston and ran for 49 more. He joined Joe Flacco and Josh McCown as the only Browns quarterbacks with 300 passing yards in three straight starts. He also led his sixth fourth-quarter go-ahead scoring drive of the season.

stories.text: 55: Straight games without allowing a 300-yard passer
stories.summary: The Browns extended the longest active streak in the NFL by holding C.J. Stroud to 211 yards, only 21 of them in the second half. Cleveland has also been outscored 78-13 in first quarters this season, the league's second-lowest first-quarter total.

stories.text: Browns return from the bye to host Las Vegas on Sunday night
stories.summary: Cleveland hosts the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, after the league flexed the game into Sunday Night Football. It is the Browns' first Sunday night home game since 2019. Watch the first quarter, where Cleveland has not scored on an opening drive all year.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers fall 19-16 in Philadelphia

stories.text: Steelers drop a 19-16 decision to the Eagles
stories.summary: Philadelphia led 13-0 and held on after Jake Elliott kicked a 55-yard field goal with 4:19 left. Max Hurleman caught a 20-yard touchdown with 1:21 to go to cut it to three, but the Steelers never got the ball back. Aaron Rodgers went 30 of 44 for 227 yards and was sacked five times, and the run game managed 73 yards on 20 carries. Pittsburgh falls to 6-4.

stories.text: Highsmith in a boot, Metcalf faces review after ejection
stories.summary: Edge rusher Alex Highsmith hurt his ankle in the first quarter and was in a protective boot Monday. Coach Mike McCarthy said it will be tough for him to play Friday, and backup Nick Herbig is already out. Receiver Michael Pittman Jr. sat out Sunday, and McCarthy is very confident he returns. DK Metcalf was ejected, and the NFL says he will not be suspended but is reviewing the play.

stories.text: Max Hurleman steps up after Metcalf's ejection
stories.summary: Hurleman, elevated from the practice squad, caught six passes for a team-high 61 yards and scored his first NFL touchdown. He took on a bigger role after Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter. Pittsburgh had only five receivers active.

stories.text: 73: Rushing yards on 20 carries as the offense stalled
stories.summary: The Steelers ran for 73 yards on 20 carries against Philadelphia and gave up five sacks. McCarthy said the team needs to get the ball to its backs more and that he takes responsibility for that. The defense played well, with three sacks and eight tackles for loss.

stories.text: Steelers host Denver on Black Friday
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts the Broncos on Friday, Nov. 27 at 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video at Acrisure Stadium, a short week. A Sunday night game against the Texans follows. Watch the edge rush if Highsmith cannot go and who lines up at receiver.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans rout Colts, eye the Ravens

stories.text: Texans run over the Colts on Thursday night
stories.summary: Houston beat Indianapolis 26-3 in Week 11 to move to 4-6. The defense forced a safety and an interception, and rookie Marlin Klein scored his first career touchdown in the third quarter. The Texans now turn to Baltimore with extra rest.

stories.text: Harrison's hamstring is called short-term
stories.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. has missed two straight games with a hamstring strain, and the team calls it relatively short-term. Woody Marks is trending the right direction from his concussion, and Danielle Hunter is making progress, according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

stories.text: Will Anderson Jr. bounces back with a safety
stories.summary: Anderson played through an ankle problem and had his worst game of the year against Cleveland. Against the Colts he piled up tackles for loss and sacked the quarterback for a safety that made it 19-3 early in the second half.

stories.text: 3: Points Houston allowed to Indianapolis
stories.summary: The Colts scored only a field goal on their opening drive and nothing after it. Jonathan Taylor carried 11 times for 21 yards, and Indianapolis waived quarterback Daniel Jones the next day.

stories.text: Ravens visit NRG Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Houston (4-6) hosts Baltimore (4-7) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch whether Harrison returns and how the run game splits carries between David Montgomery and Marks.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts cut Jones, hand job to Richardson

stories.text: Colts waive Daniel Jones, start Anthony Richardson
stories.summary: Indianapolis cut Jones a day after the 26-3 loss in Houston. Jones led the league with 13 interceptions in 11 starts. Richardson, the 2023 fourth overall pick, starts for the first time since Week 16 of 2024.

stories.text: Pierce stays on IR, McGowan out with hamstring
stories.summary: Receiver Alec Pierce will not come off injured reserve and is done for the season, per Ian Rapoport. Running back Seth McGowan will miss time with a hamstring injury, and coach Shane Steichen gave no return date.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor stays quiet and stays put
stories.summary: Taylor managed 21 yards on 11 carries against Houston. Reports say the Colts turned down an offer of a second-round pick and more for him, so he remains in Indianapolis.

stories.text: 13: Interceptions Jones threw in 11 starts
stories.summary: That total led the NFL. Jones also ranked last among 31 qualifiers in QBR, yards per attempt and yards per dropback. He finished with 12 of 27 for 144 yards against Houston.

stories.text: Giants visit Indianapolis on Sunday
stories.summary: The Colts (3-8) host New York on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Richardson makes his first start in nearly two years, and Steichen says Riley Leonard could also play.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars regroup after red zone stumble

stories.text: Giants beat Jaguars 23-18, snapping a three-game streak
stories.summary: Jacksonville (7-3) kept the AFC South lead but scored one touchdown on six red zone trips. Coach Liam Coen said his team was outplayed and outcoached in all three phases and held an accountability meeting on Monday.

stories.text: Tuten limited after ankle gets stepped on twice
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten aggravated his ankle against the Giants. Coen said Monday's recheck was not too bad and expects Tuten to be limited again. The team will watch him Wednesday and Thursday. Tackle Walker Little also left in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Josh Hines-Allen sacks and strips in a loss
stories.summary: Hines-Allen finished with five tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit. He also forced the Cam Skattebo fumble that gave Jacksonville its best scoring chance of the third quarter.

stories.text: 13: Penalties the Jaguars took for 107 yards
stories.summary: The Giants were flagged six times for 46 yards. Jacksonville also scored no rushing touchdown for the first time since its loss to Houston in Week 6, and Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions.

stories.text: Titans visit EverBank Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville hosts Tennessee (1-9) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX in the Salute to Service game. The Jaguars beat the Titans 40-23 on Nov. 15, and the Tennessee defense has allowed 40 or more points in three straight games.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Saleh rips defense after 51-30 loss

stories.text: Saleh says he has '100%' support after 1-9 start
stories.summary: Coach Robert Saleh told reporters he has full backing from owner Amy Adams Strunk after a 51-30 loss at Dallas. The defense is last in the NFL in yards allowed at 399.8 per game, and opponents have scored on 13 straight drives.

stories.text: Secondary and left tackle banged up
stories.summary: Safety Tony Adams left with an illness and had no update Monday. Cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (neck), safety Terrell Burgess (knee) and left tackle Dan Moore Jr. (knee) are also on the list.

stories.text: Cam Ward keeps producing in the losses
stories.summary: Ward went 21 of 30 for 248 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions at Dallas, though a sack-fumble hurt. He has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three straight games, and Saleh still calls him the starter.

stories.text: 134: Points Tennessee allowed in three games
stories.summary: The Titans have also given up 1,449 yards over that span. The 51 points against Dallas were the most they have allowed since Detroit scored 52 in October 2024. Saleh said the problem is execution, not personnel.

stories.text: Titans travel to Jacksonville on Sunday
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at the 7-3 Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX after a flex move. The Titans lost the first meeting 40-23 on Nov. 15, and Jacksonville is the division leader.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos run past Raiders for sixth straight win

stories.text: Broncos beat Raiders 38-24 for a sixth straight win
stories.summary: Denver built a 17-point lead, watched it vanish in the third quarter, then closed the game on the ground and with a pick-six. The Broncos sit at 8-2, level with Kansas City atop the AFC West.

stories.text: No new Broncos injuries after the Raiders game
stories.summary: Neither ESPN nor Bleacher Report listed an injury from Denver's win over Las Vegas. Check the first Friday practice report before the short week at Pittsburgh.

stories.text: Jonah Coleman runs for 111 yards and three touchdowns
stories.summary: The rookie carried 24 times and added four catches for 18 yards. It was his first 100-yard game. He is the first Broncos rookie with that rushing line since Clinton Portis in 2002.

stories.text: 43.2%: Denver's blitz rate against Fernando Mendoza
stories.summary: That was the second-highest blitz rate of the Broncos' season. Mendoza went down four times when they brought extra rushers, and Ja'Quan McMillian closed the game with a pick-six.

stories.text: Broncos visit Steelers on Black Friday at 3 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Denver plays at Acrisure Stadium on Friday, Nov. 27, on Prime Video. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph wants fewer big plays after Las Vegas hit three of 30 yards or more.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Mahomes and Kelce lead 34-7 rout of Cardinals

stories.text: Chiefs score on first five drives in 34-7 win over Cardinals
stories.summary: Kansas City won its third straight and fell to second in the AFC West only because Denver also won. The defense has now held opponents to 13 points or fewer three weeks running.

stories.text: Walker sat with a groin injury, Smith in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Running back Kenneth Walker III missed the game with a groin injury and is close to returning. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (right ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) were also listed.

stories.text: Kelce catches two touchdowns as Mahomes tops 300 yards
stories.summary: Mahomes went 27 of 39 for 324 yards and three touchdowns, his second straight 300-yard game. Travis Kelce caught six passes for 74 yards and two scores, and rookie Emmett Johnson ran for 105 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 110: Kelce's career touchdowns, third among tight ends
stories.summary: Kelce's two scores moved him past Jimmy Graham for fourth in touchdown catches by a tight end with 90. His 110 total touchdowns, counting playoffs, rank third at the position.

stories.text: Chiefs play at Bills on Thanksgiving night, 8:20 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The game airs on NBC on Thursday, Nov. 26. Kansas City then faces road games at the Rams and Bengals.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza's pick-six ends Raiders' rally in Denver

stories.text: Raiders fall to 4-7 as a pick-six seals 38-24 loss in Denver
stories.summary: Las Vegas cut a 17-point deficit in the third quarter, but Fernando Mendoza threw an interception that Ja'Quan McMillian returned for a touchdown on the final drive. The Raiders sit tenth in the AFC wild-card race.

stories.text: Brock Bowers misses the Denver game with ankle and quad issues
stories.summary: The Raiders played without their top pass catcher. ESPN lists an ankle and quad problem for Bowers, who did not play. Watch his practice status ahead of Sunday night at Cleveland.

stories.text: Rookie Mendoza throws three touchdowns in loss
stories.summary: Mendoza completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. His first career touchdown pass went 68 yards to Ashton Jeanty, and Jack Bech caught eight passes for 88 yards and a score.

stories.text: 435: yards Eric Stokes allowed before Week 11
stories.summary: Stokes gave up 35 catches for 435 yards and a 112.6 passer rating entering the Denver game, per ESPN. Coach Klint Kubiak criticized his effort the week before, and Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter and Hezekiah Masses have rotated in.

stories.text: Raiders visit Browns on Sunday Night Football, 8:20 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The NFL flexed the Nov. 29 game to NBC from a 1 p.m. start. Cleveland is 6-4 and holds the last AFC playoff spot entering Week 11.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Herbert enters concussion protocol after Jets loss

stories.text: Chargers lose 27-24 to Jets and fall to 1-9
stories.summary: Los Angeles had just won its first game of the season the week before. Justin Herbert threw two touchdowns with no interceptions, but the line gave up six sacks and the Chargers could not catch up.

stories.text: Herbert enters concussion protocol after the Jets game
stories.summary: The quarterback entered the concussion protocol after the 27-24 loss. His status for Sunday's game against New England has not been announced in the sources reviewed.

stories.text: McConkey scores twice in his return from a back injury
stories.summary: Ladd McConkey missed two games with a back injury and came back with two touchdown catches, including Herbert's late fourth-quarter throw. Herbert threw for 131 yards and added a rushing touchdown.

stories.text: 60.0%: Herbert's sack rate on pressures against the Jets
stories.summary: The Jets pressured Herbert 10 times and sacked him six times. That is the highest pressure-to-sack rate of his career.

stories.text: Chargers host Patriots on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The NFL moved the game out of primetime. New England is 5-5 and has lost three of its last four, and quarterback Drake Maye is out indefinitely with a right ankle injury.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys hang 51 on Titans before Thanksgiving

stories.text: Cowboys score on every drive in 51-30 rout of Titans
stories.summary: Dallas scored a touchdown on each of its first six possessions and beat Tennessee 51-30 on Sunday to move to 5-6. The offense scored on every drive except the final kneel-down. The defense still gave up 30 points, and Carnell Tate's 59-yard touchdown exposed tackling and coverage problems the Cowboys need to fix by Thursday.

stories.text: Winters leaves with knee contusion, Barham out
stories.summary: Linebacker Dee Winters left the Titans game with a knee contusion and did not return. The team does not appear worried about his long-term status, but linebacker depth is thin with Jaishawn Barham out. Tight end Jake Ferguson has missed two games with ankle and knee problems and is a status to watch on the short week.

stories.text: Prescott throws for 325 and four scores, adds a rushing TD
stories.summary: Dak Prescott went 28 of 33 for 325 yards and four touchdowns, and he ran for another score. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a touchdown, and George Pickens added seven catches for 102 yards and a score. It was the first time this season both receivers topped 100 yards in the same game.

stories.text: 6: straight 1,000-yard seasons for CeeDee Lamb
stories.summary: Lamb became the first receiver in Cowboys history with six consecutive 1,000-yard seasons when he topped the mark against Tennessee. He finished with 11 catches for 132 yards and a touchdown, and he played 56 of the Cowboys' 65 offensive snaps.

stories.text: Eagles visit Dallas on Thanksgiving Day
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Philadelphia on Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. A win would put the Cowboys at .500 and leave the Eagles a half game behind them. Former Cowboys practice-squad quarterback Joe Milton starts for Philadelphia, and Brian Schottenheimer says he expects Milton to know the Dallas defense well.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants beat Jaguars, hold NFC East lead

stories.text: Giants beat Jaguars 23-18 and stay atop the NFC East
stories.summary: New York improved to 6-3-1 with a 23-18 win over Jacksonville at MetLife Stadium, ending the Jaguars' three-game win streak. It was the Giants' first win over a team with a winning record this season. Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions, and Jacksonville went 1 for 6 in the red zone.

stories.text: Newsome out multiple weeks with high ankle sprain
stories.summary: Cornerback Greg Newsome II left the Jaguars game with an ankle injury, and John Harbaugh called it a serious high ankle sprain on Monday. Newsome will miss multiple weeks, and Harbaugh said it is too early to decide on surgery. Paulson Adebo and Dru Phillips played well after Newsome went down.

stories.text: Abdul Carter piles up two sacks and five QB hits
stories.summary: Carter set career highs with two sacks and five quarterback hits against Jacksonville, and Harbaugh said he dominated the game. The edge rusher also finished with two tackles for loss. The Giants held the Jaguars to 5 of 15 on third down.

stories.text: 12: pressures for Abdul Carter against Jacksonville
stories.summary: Carter generated a career-high 12 pressures, the second most by any player in a game this season, including six quick pressures. He turned them into two sacks. Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions as the Giants' front kept him off balance all game.

stories.text: Giants visit the 3-8 Colts on Sunday
stories.summary: New York travels to Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET. The Colts are 3-8. The Giants will likely be without Newsome and get six days of rest, while the Colts have nine.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles end skid, head to Dallas on Thanksgiving

stories.text: Eagles beat Steelers 19-16 for first win since Week 2
stories.summary: Philadelphia snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh at Lincoln Financial Field and moved to 3-7. Joe Milton earned his first career win as a starter. The Eagles blew a 13-3 halftime lead but held on after the defense stopped the Steelers on a goal-to-go series.

stories.text: Baun to IR, Mitchell out with hamstring injury
stories.summary: Linebacker Zack Baun went on injured reserve, and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell left the Steelers game with a hamstring injury. Jonathan Jones was also hurt on a late play. Saquon Barkley's issue is unclear: NFL.com reported a shoulder problem late in the game, while an estimated Monday report listed him limited with neck and illness. Jalen Hurts has not played since Week 5 because of blood clots in his calf.

stories.text: Barkley runs for 75 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley carried 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown against Pittsburgh, including a 38-yard run. Joe Milton completed 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards without a turnover. Milton also made the game-clinching first-down throw to DeVonta Smith.

stories.text: 5: sacks of Aaron Rodgers by the Eagles' defense
stories.summary: Philadelphia sacked Rodgers five times and recorded 14 tackles for loss in the win. Byron Young had two of the sacks. The Eagles won despite holding the ball for only 24:30, against 35:30 for Pittsburgh.

stories.text: Eagles visit the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day
stories.summary: Philadelphia plays at Dallas on Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. A win would leave the Eagles a half game behind the Cowboys in the NFC East. Milton, a former Dallas practice-squad quarterback, starts again, and the Eagles are 3.5 games behind first-place New York.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders stun Bengals on last-second field goal

stories.text: Commanders beat Bengals 22-20 on a walk-off field goal
stories.summary: Drew Stevens kicked the winning field goal as time expired on Monday night, ending Cincinnati's five-game win streak. Washington moved 64 yards in 34 seconds on the final drive after the Bengals took the lead late. The Commanders are 4-5-1 with their second straight win and sit two games behind the Giants.

stories.text: Croskey-Merritt returns from IR and scores
stories.summary: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt came off injured reserve with a groin injury on Monday and scored a 1-yard touchdown before halftime. He finished with 13 carries for 54 yards. Rachaad White (heel) and Amik Robertson (ankle) carried questionable designations into the game, and the Commanders reported no new injuries afterward.

stories.text: Rookie Antonio Williams catches 9 for 122 yards
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Antonio Williams caught nine passes for 122 yards, and two long throws from Jayden Daniels in the final drive set up the winning kick. Daniels threw for roughly 285 yards (sources list 283 and 289) and ran for 55 more. Boye Mafe of Cincinnati sacked him three times in the first half.

stories.text: 31: rushing yards allowed by Washington's defense
stories.summary: The Commanders held Cincinnati to 31 rushing yards on 14 carries. Joe Burrow completed 8 of 16 passes for 59 yards by ESPN's count, though another report credits him with 300 passing yards. Stevens went 5 for 5 on field goals.

stories.text: Commanders visit the Cardinals on Sunday
stories.summary: Washington plays at Arizona on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The Commanders have won two straight and three of their last four. Watch whether the run defense that shut down Cincinnati travels west.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Simmons sacks Saints three times, Bears win five

stories.text: Bears beat Saints 21-13 for fifth straight win
stories.summary: Chicago built a 16-0 lead at Soldier Field, let New Orleans cut it to six by halftime, then shut the door with a safety from Montez Sweat in the fourth quarter. The Bears are 8-2 and travel to Detroit on Thursday with first place in the NFC North on the line. They are 0-2 in the division so far.

stories.text: Roschon Johnson leaves with ankle injury
stories.summary: Running back Roschon Johnson went out in the first quarter against the Saints with an ankle injury. Offensive lineman Theo Benedet also left late in the fourth quarter. The Bears have a short week before Thursday at Detroit, so the first practice report will show who has a chance to play.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons ties career high with three sacks
stories.summary: Simmons took down Tyler Shough three times, matching his career best for one game. He has five sacks in three games since Chicago acquired him from Tennessee on Oct. 29. Caleb Williams finished 15 of 23 for 181 yards with two touchdowns and one interception.

stories.text: 6: Sacks the Bears put on Tyler Shough
stories.summary: The Bears sacked Shough six times and logged 23 quarterback pressures. Simmons had three of the sacks, and Sweat's came in the end zone for a safety. Clark Phillips III forced a fumble that Austin Booker recovered.

stories.text: Bears visit Lions on Thanksgiving with first place at stake
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Ford Field on Thursday, Nov. 26 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The winner takes the NFC North lead. Coach Ben Johnson is looking for his first win over Detroit, and the Lions will play without edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions win sixth straight, host Bears Thursday

stories.text: Lions beat Buccaneers 31-21 without Hutchinson
stories.summary: Detroit won its sixth straight game in its first outing without Aidan Hutchinson. Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes, Jahmyr Gibbs ran for two scores in the fourth quarter, and the defense sacked Baker Mayfield on back-to-back late series to seal it. The Lions are 8-2 and host Chicago on Thanksgiving.

stories.text: Hutchinson out for season, Jack Campbell sidelined
stories.summary: Hutchinson hurt his right knee celebrating a sack in the Week 10 win over New England, and an AP source said the injury ends his season. Rookie Derrick Moore, a second-round pick, is the first option to replace him. Linebacker Jack Campbell has a severe neck injury with no return date.

stories.text: Goff hits 279 yards, no turnovers against Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Goff went 20 of 28 for 279 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, good for a 126.9 passer rating. His 57-yard touchdown to Jameson Williams was the long play, and Williams finished with four catches for 93 yards. Goff also converted a third-and-9 with his legs.

stories.text: 98: Gibbs rushing yards against the NFL's top run defense
stories.summary: Gibbs gained 98 yards and scored twice against a Tampa Bay defense ranked first against the run. Detroit's pass rush produced fewer pressures than it did against New England, which is the question heading into Thanksgiving without Hutchinson.

stories.text: Lions host Bears on Thanksgiving for the division lead
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Chicago on Thursday, Nov. 26 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Ford Field. Both teams are 8-2. Watch the Detroit pass rush without Hutchinson and how Gibbs fares against a Bears run defense that allows about 91 yards per game.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Parsons cleared to debut Wednesday at the Rams

stories.text: Parsons cleared to make season debut against Rams
stories.summary: Micah Parsons has been medically cleared and is expected to play Wednesday night, 347 days after he tore his ACL and meniscus. He still needs final clearance from his surgeon and must come off the physically unable to perform list. Expect a snap count.

stories.text: Packers carry several bumps into Rams game
stories.summary: As of Nov. 16, right guard Kevin Zeitler had a triceps injury that kept him from his first start of the year. Receiver Bo Melton (thigh) and cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib) drew no concern from coach Matt LaFleur, and Skyy Moore (ankle) was still being evaluated. Parsons remains on the PUP list until the team activates him.

stories.text: Parsons set to return after 12.5 sacks last year
stories.summary: Parsons played 14 games last season and led Green Bay with 12.5 sacks. He also led the NFL with 64 pressures, according to ESPN Analytics. He began practicing Nov. 4 and added 11-on-11 work the next week.

stories.text: 8: Sacks Minnesota put on Jordan Love
stories.summary: The Vikings sacked Love eight times in their 30-10 win in Week 10, the most Green Bay has allowed since 2015. The Packers also lost three fumbles, and each one led to a Minnesota field goal. Love finished 17 of 27 for 220 yards.

stories.text: Packers visit Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix after the bye. The Packers are 6-4, last in the NFC North, and tied with the Rams and Seahawks for the final playoff spot. Watch Parsons' snap count and the pass protection after the eight-sack game.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings fall 35-10 in Mexico City, lose Darrisaw

stories.text: 49ers rout Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City
stories.summary: Brock Purdy threw three touchdown passes and Ji'Ayir Brown returned a Kirk Cousins interception for a score as San Francisco pulled away. The Vikings fell to 7-3 and sit third in the NFC North, one game behind Detroit and Chicago. Thursday's Bears-Lions game will move one of those teams back toward them.

stories.text: Darrisaw leaves with right shoulder injury
stories.summary: Left tackle Christian Darrisaw hurt his right shoulder, came back after halftime and then left for good. Coach Kevin O'Connell said it is a different shoulder from the one that bothered him in early November. Ryan Van Demark took over at left tackle, and Wednesday's practice report is the first read for Sunday against Atlanta.

stories.text: Cousins throws pick-six in tough Vikings night
stories.summary: Cousins completed 26 of 38 passes for 235 yards, but his interception returned 18 yards for a touchdown broke the game open. It was his second loss to San Francisco in three weeks, after a pick-six for the Raiders against the 49ers in Week 9. The Vikings had acquired him from Las Vegas at the trade deadline.

stories.text: 31: Points the Vikings have scored in their three losses
stories.summary: Minnesota managed 10 against San Francisco, and the offense has scored 31 points combined in its three defeats. The Vikings also ran for just 69 yards on 21 carries. The defense still allows the fewest points in the division.

stories.text: Vikings host Falcons on Sunday
stories.summary: Minnesota is home against Atlanta on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET at U.S. Bank Stadium. Watch the left tackle spot and whether the run game finds room. Detroit visits U.S. Bank Stadium on Dec. 20.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons use the bye to self scout a 3-game skid

stories.text: Falcons enter the bye looking for answers on offense
stories.summary: Atlanta lost 35-13 to Kansas City on Nov. 15, its third straight loss and fifth in six games. Michael Penix Jr. has one touchdown and six interceptions in the three November losses, and the offense scored 30 points total in that stretch. Kevin Stefanski called the bye a time for a self scout, and Tommy Rees keeps the play calling.

stories.text: Branch and Deablo were the last names on the Falcons list
stories.summary: Receiver Zachariah Branch was ruled out with a hamstring injury for the second straight game before the bye. Linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) was doubtful, and edge James Pearce Jr. (back) was questionable. Atlanta had not released a post-bye status for any of them as of Tuesday.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson says the boos were deserved
stories.summary: Robinson ran 16 times for 71 yards against the Chiefs. He has not reached 20 carries since the Week 7 win over San Francisco, and he missed that mark in all five losses in the last six games. After the game he said the fans were right to boo the team.

stories.text: 4: straight three-and-outs to open the Chiefs game
stories.summary: Atlanta started the Kansas City game with four consecutive three-and-outs, its first start like that since 2000. The Falcons also went 5 for 16 on third down and 1 for 5 in the red zone. They averaged a league-high 31 points per game from Weeks 3 to 7.

stories.text: Falcons visit the Vikings after the bye
stories.summary: Atlanta plays at Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Then comes a home game against Detroit on Dec. 6. Stefanski wants the offense to stay on schedule against Brian Flores' defense.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers beat Ravens 35-33, lead NFC South by two

stories.text: Fitzgerald's field goal lifts Panthers past Ravens, 35-33
stories.summary: Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left, and Tyrel Dodson intercepted Jacoby Brissett's last heave with 33 seconds to go. Carolina is 5-5 and two games clear in the NFC South with seven left. It is the Panthers' first two-game division lead since the end of 2015.

stories.text: Coker clears concussion protocol; Horn still waits
stories.summary: Receiver Jalen Coker cleared the concussion protocol after a late hit against Baltimore, and Dave Canales said he is good to go. Cornerback Jaycee Horn has not opened his practice window yet. Tackle Brady Christensen has practiced for three weeks, so the team must activate him or move him to injured reserve.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard runs for 120 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Hubbard carried 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns against the Ravens. He became the second Panther after Christian McCaffrey to reach 1,000 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in six games this year.

stories.text: 14: game-winning drives for Bryce Young
stories.summary: Young led the 14th game-winning drive of his career against Baltimore. He threw for 254 yards and two touchdowns. Carolina has now won two straight to get back to .500.

stories.text: Panthers visit Tampa Bay on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Carolina plays at Tampa Bay on Monday, Nov. 30 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bucs beat the Panthers 43-13 in Charlotte in Week 7, so Carolina has a score to settle and a division lead to protect.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints fall 21-13 in Chicago as offense stalls again

stories.text: Saints drop a fifth one-score game, 21-13 at Chicago
stories.summary: New Orleans scored nothing in the first or third quarter and fell to 3-7, its third loss in four games. Tyler Shough was sacked six times, including a safety, and the Saints turned two takeaways into zero points. Kellen Moore said the team battled but could not score enough.

stories.text: Juwan Johnson's hamstring is the one to watch
stories.summary: Tight end Juwan Johnson hurt his hamstring against the Bears and is still being evaluated. Moore expects a clearer picture Wednesday, when the Saints hold their first Week 12 practice. If Johnson sits, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp pick up more snaps. Cornerback Quincy Riley also left with a bicep injury.

stories.text: Chris Olave posts 9 catches for 102 yards in a loss
stories.summary: Olave led both teams in receptions and yards at Soldier Field, one of the few steady spots for a Saints offense that never found a rhythm. Rookie Jordyn Tyson caught one pass for six yards.

stories.text: 9: first-quarter points all season, fewest in the NFL
stories.summary: The Saints have scored nine points in the first quarter through 10 games, the lowest total in the league. Another slow start in Chicago put them down 16-0 before they cut it to six by halftime.

stories.text: Saints head to Cincinnati for a Week 12 road game
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. It is the second game of a two-game road stretch. Watch whether the offense scores early and whether Shough gets cleaner protection.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs fall to Lions 31-21, trail Carolina by two

stories.text: Lions pull away from the Bucs, 31-21
stories.summary: Tampa Bay trailed by three entering the fourth quarter, then Jahmyr Gibbs scored twice and Detroit won at Ford Field. The Bucs are 3-7 and two games behind first-place Carolina. Todd Bowles said his team shot itself in the foot, and Baker Mayfield said the Bucs are out of mulligans.

stories.text: Two starting corners head for MRIs
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Jacob Parrish (back) and Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) both left the Detroit game and did not return. Bowles said both would get MRIs on Monday and the team would know more on severity afterward. Mayfield played through a foot injury.

stories.text: Rookie Ted Hurst III catches two touchdowns
stories.summary: Hurst caught five passes for 56 yards and two touchdowns from Mayfield, one before halftime and one late in the fourth quarter. They were his second and third scores of the season.

stories.text: 80: yards on a Bucky Irving run erased by a penalty
stories.summary: A holding call on Luke Goedeke wiped out what looked like an 80-yard Irving touchdown. Irving still finished with 100 scrimmage yards, 68 rushing and 32 receiving, and a 1-yard score. Mayfield was sacked four times.

stories.text: Bucs host Carolina on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. A win would cut Carolina's division lead to one game and give the Bucs the season sweep after their 43-13 win in Week 7. Watch the cornerback depth if Parrish and Morrison miss time.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals drop 34-7 at Kansas City

stories.text: Chiefs rout Cardinals 34-7 as Josh Johnson starts at QB
stories.summary: Arizona fell to 3-8 at Arrowhead. Patrick Mahomes threw for 324 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to Travis Kelce, and Kansas City outgained the Cardinals 435 yards to 205. Josh Johnson, a 40-year-old journeyman, went 18 of 31 for 155 yards in place of the injured Carson Beck.

stories.text: Beck's back still a question, Paris Johnson Jr. sidelined
stories.summary: Rookie quarterback Carson Beck sat out Sunday with back spasms, and his status for Washington remains unclear. Left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. missed the game, while Jayden Williams returned from a multi-week knee injury. Guard Jon Gaines, out five weeks with an ankle injury, could be an option if he is healthy.

stories.text: Undrafted rookie Harrison Wallace III leads Arizona receivers
stories.summary: Wallace caught four passes for a team-high 57 yards on seven targets, including a 25-yard grab that was the Cardinals' longest play of the day. Coach Mike LaFleur praised the undrafted rookie after the game. Trey McBride caught nine passes for 54 yards on 14 targets.

stories.text: 11: straight home losses for Arizona, a 427-day streak
stories.summary: The Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Nov. 15 was their 11th straight at home, and the streak now stretches 427 days. The league record is 14, set by the 1988-89 Cowboys and the 2008-2010 Rams. Arizona hosts Washington next at State Farm Stadium.

stories.text: Cardinals host Washington on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: Arizona plays Washington at State Farm Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Watch the quarterback decision between Beck and Johnson, and whether the line can keep the pocket clean after allowing three sacks in Kansas City. Arizona has a bye in Week 14.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams lose Nacua before Packers game

stories.text: Puka Nacua out after MCL surgery and a three-game suspension
stories.summary: Nacua had surgery on an MCL injury last week, and Sean McVay said he will miss a couple of months. The NFL also suspended him three games for a personal conduct policy violation, and he is eligible for reinstatement Dec. 14. The Rams are 6-4 on a four-game win streak.

stories.text: Avila out, Curl in doubt, Kyren Williams limited
stories.summary: In the first injury report of Week 12, guard Steve Avila (hamstring) did not participate and will not play, and safety Kam Curl (toe) is in doubt. Center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) is out for several weeks. Running back Kyren Williams (toe) was limited, and Kobie Turner (groin) was a full participant and is expected to play.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards without the top two receivers
stories.summary: Corum rushed for 100 yards and scored from a yard out in the 34-6 win over Arizona. Matthew Stafford threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns, to Tyler Higbee, Xavier Smith and Davis Allen. Nacua and Davante Adams were both out.

stories.text: 1:06: all it took the Rams to flip a 6-3 deficit into 17-6
stories.summary: Los Angeles trailed Arizona 6-3 late in the second quarter, then scored twice in the final 1:06 of the half to lead 17-6 at the break. The Rams finished with a 34-6 win, their fourth in a row. Arizona managed 123 total yards.

stories.text: Rams host Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, 8 PM ET on Netflix
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts Green Bay on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at SoFi Stadium, with an 8 PM ET kickoff on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4. Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons has been medically cleared to make his season debut, so the Rams' offensive line faces a test.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers hit 9-1 with 35-10 win in Mexico City

stories.text: 49ers beat Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City for 9-1 start
stories.summary: San Francisco improved to 9-1 on Sunday night with three first-half touchdown passes from Brock Purdy. Ji'Ayir Brown returned an interception for a touchdown, and Deommodore Lenoir forced and recovered a Justin Jefferson fumble to open the second half. Kyle Shanahan earned his 100th career win, postseason included.

stories.text: Right tackle Colton McKivitz likely done for the year
stories.summary: McKivitz suffered a broken and dislocated left ankle in the second quarter, and Shanahan called the injury crushing. He had started 61 straight games. Vederian Lowe takes over at right tackle for the rest of the season. Receiver Mike Evans returned from Achilles tendinitis in the win.

stories.text: George Kittle scores twice on three catches
stories.summary: Kittle caught three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns, from 17 and 8 yards out, in the first half in Mexico City. Mike Evans added six catches for 109 yards and a score in his return, and Christian McCaffrey scored for the eighth straight game.

stories.text: 10-0: Purdy's record when he posts a 140-plus passer rating
stories.summary: Purdy went 21 of 26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions, a 146.0 passer rating. He now has 10 career games with a rating of 140 or better in his first five seasons, the most in NFL history, and the 49ers are 10-0 in them.

stories.text: Seahawks visit Levi's Stadium Sunday at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: San Francisco hosts Seattle on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. The Seahawks (6-4) are three games back in the NFC West and could get quarterback Sam Darnold back from a quad injury. The 49ers won the first meeting in October at Lumen Field.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Darnold decision looms before the 49ers

stories.text: Darnold on track to start at San Francisco, decision Wednesday
stories.summary: Sam Darnold has missed two games with a quad injury and took part in a bonus walk-through-tempo practice Monday. Mike Macdonald says he is still on track to start Sunday against the 49ers, with the final call coming after Wednesday's practice. Backup Drew Lock is 4-0 as a starter this season.

stories.text: Offensive line thinned out, George Holani to injured reserve
stories.summary: Right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle sprain) left the Raiders game, left guard Quenton Nelson is recovering from a knee procedure, and right guard Anthony Bradford has a knee injury. Running back George Holani went on injured reserve, and defensive tackle Leonard Williams missed two games with a stinger. Seattle promoted Trevon Diggs and Bobby Hart from the practice squad.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 1,207 yards and no rival at 1,000
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 171 yards and a 71-yard touchdown in the 21-13 win at Las Vegas. He has 79 catches, 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns with seven games left. No other NFL receiver has reached 1,000 yards, and CeeDee Lamb is next at 976.

stories.text: 144: Smith-Njigba yards in one quarter, a Seahawks record
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba piled up 144 receiving yards in the third quarter against the Raiders, a franchise record for a single quarter. He finished with 171 yards. Seattle won 21-13 and is 4-0 in games Drew Lock has played this season.

stories.text: Seahawks at 49ers, Sunday 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Seattle was off in Week 11 and plays at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. San Francisco won the first meeting in October. Watch the quarterback call and whether the offensive line can hold up against the NFC West leader.
